tokens.content: NeuroCare AI is a university software and machine-learning project that demonstrates classification of a diabetes-related label in a historical public health survey. It connects a React/TypeScript interface, a FastAPI service, a TensorFlow/Keras artificial neural network (ANN), and PostgreSQL persistence. Users enter a fictional profile containing 21 coded survey features, review their answers, and receive the model's class, score, version and decision threshold after a database save. The application is an educational prototype, not a diagnostic, screening or individual future-risk tool.

tokens.content: The configured model uses a processed cohort of 222,600 BRFSS 2021 records. Its ANN has two hidden dense layers of 64 and 32 units and a sigmoid output. On 40,376 previously evaluated test records, the model achieves 67.04% accuracy, 29.78% precision, 82.82% recall and ROC AUC 0.8129. F1, calculated for this report from the saved confusion matrix, is 0.4381. These results indicate useful ranking of survey labels within this cohort but substantial classification errors: 1,076 positive labels are missed and 12,231 negative labels are flagged positive. They do not establish clinical validity or reliable performance in another population.
